title: Slim control-plane row payloads and reshuffle indexes by heuristic
creator: Owen Li
description: Problem: Control plane queries are being dominated by a small set of wide rows that contain JSONB blobs and historical audit payloads. These wide rows increase IO, bloat indexes, and trigger frequent heap & index scans for tenant-facing queries. Goal: Reduce average row width for hot tables (projects, tenants, control_events) and reorganize indexes using an access-frequency heuristic so hot OLTP paths use compact indexes and cold fields are archived.
acceptance_criteria: P50 query latency for tenant metadata lookups reduced by >=30% on staging
Average row width for targeted tables reduced by >=40% after backfill
New partial indexes demonstrably cover 95% of hot queries in production traces
All migrations can be rolled back with documented steps and no downtime for read/write workloads
migration_plan: 1) Add compact columns (proto fields: owner_id, status_code, small_attrs) alongside existing JSONB. 2) Implement staged backfill worker that copies slices with rate limits and verifies checksums. 3) Introduce partial indexes on (owner_id, status_code) and bloom indexes for high-cardinality attributes. 4) Add histogram telemetry for row width and index hit ratios to Grafana. 5) Switch application read paths to prefer compact columns behind a feature flag. 6) Drop JSONB fields after 2-week verification window.
safety_and_rollback: Backfill worker runs with tenant throttling; all schema changes are additive. We will use a pre-migration shadow table if needed. Rollback: disable feature flag to resume reads from JSONB, run a compact-to-json copy if partial rows were read, and re-open access. Full rollback steps documented in runbook.
notes: We chose a frequency-weighted heuristic for index reshuffle: compute per-column access count from pg_stat_statements and recent query traces, then select prefix columns that cover >=90% of accesses but keep index width under 3 columns where possible. This reduces index bloat and improves cache locality.
